name: archive
algorithm: Create a signed, sealed archive of a directory tree: walk it, sort the files by path, read and SHA-256 each one, DEFLATE them as one stream, sign the manifest with Ed25519 and seal the archive with AES-256-GCM under fixed test keys; then, untimed, open it again, verifying the seal, the signature and every file's digest (README.md).

rust.name: sha2
rust.inside: unsafe Rust and the x86 SHA extensions (sha256rnds2) through core::arch, chosen at run time by cpufeatures 0.2.17, with a software fallback; digest 0.10.7, block-buffer 0.10.4, crypto-common 0.1.7, generic-array 0.14.7 and typenum 1.20.0

rust.name: flate2
rust.inside: a few unsafe blocks; its default back end miniz_oxide 0.8.8 (pure Rust, forbid(unsafe_code)) with adler2 2.0.0, and crc32fast 1.4.2 (unsafe Rust and SIMD, unused by raw DEFLATE)

rust.name: ring
rust.inside: BoringSSL-derived C and pregenerated x86_64 assembly (AES-NI, PCLMULQDQ and VAES/AVX2 AES-GCM, chosen at run time from CPUID), built by its build script with cc 1.11.0; untrusted 0.9.0, getrandom 0.2.17, cfg-if 1.0.5, and windows-sys 0.52.0

rust.name: walkdir
rust.inside: same-file 1.0.6 and winapi-util 0.1.11 (unsafe Rust calling Windows through windows-sys 0.61.2)

labels.zig: software AES, GHASH and SHA-256: Zig 0.17 chooses the crypto instructions at compile time, and the row's x86-64-v2 target has none (README.md, Hardware paths)

skip.c: no std hash, compression or cryptography in C, and no C crypto library is vendored (zlib alone would leave a partial task)

notes: The checksum is the SHA-256 of `open`'s stdout on the column's own archive (output check then, D-841): the manifest of names, sizes and SHA-256 digests and a summary line. The archive's bytes differ by DEFLATE encoder and are never compared; verify also runs every column's open on every other column's archive, and each must print the checksum (README.md, Checksum).

Hardware paths at the row's x86-64-v2 target: mk, rust (ring and sha2) and go choose AES-NI, PCLMULQDQ and SHA at run time; Zig 0.17 chooses them at compile time from the target, which has none of them, so the zig cells run software AES, GHASH and SHA-256 (README.md, Hardware paths).
Each column compresses at its library's default level; the publish-size archives differ by 1.2 percent at most (README.md, DEFLATE effort).
